clue.text: Boy with girlfriend is in French musical party

indicators.note: tells you to translate 'is' into French

parts.note: GF is the usual short form of girlfriend

explanation.surface: A boy and his girlfriend turn up at a French party with music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In French' seems to say where the party is, but it only turns 'is' into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: A songfest is a gathering where people sing together, a musical party.

clue.text: First pair of questions in National Curriculum assessment exercises

indicators.note: take the first two letters of 'questions'

parts.note: SATs are the national tests given in English schools

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is surrounded by it

explanation.surface: A school test whose first two questions are about exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: SATs are the national tests given to children in English schools under the National Curriculum. QU goes in after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Squats are a common leg exercise.

clue.text: Fundamental parts in clue edited

indicators.note: an edited text has had its letters changed around

explanation.surface: Someone editing a crossword clue finds its most important parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclei are cores or central parts, the fundamental parts of atoms or cells.

clue.text: Excellent start, performing in sack

indicators.note: letters that are performing are acting out a new arrangement

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
START rearranged, placed after FIR in FIRE

explanation.surface: A great beginning, with a show put on in a sack race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' is a verb here: to fire. FIR + STRAT + E.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate means of the best quality, excellent.

clue.text: A lot of sheepdogs flit about showing maximum pace?

indicators.note: most, but not all, of 'sheepdogs': the last letter goes
the letters are moved about

parts.note: added to the fodder, 12 letters in all

explanation.surface: Sheepdogs darting around a field at top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: the speed of light is the top speed in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Nothing can travel faster than the speed of light, so it is the maximum pace.

clue.text: Endlessly ask and ask for yoga positions

indicators.note: each word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone keeps asking and asking for yoga poses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' applies to all three words, not just the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Asana is the Sanskrit word for a seated or held posture, so yoga positions is a plain translation.

clue.text: Hackneyed opening in short story

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tired, clichéd first line in a short story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short story' reads as one phrase, but 'short' only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale ideas or phrases are worn out, hackneyed.

clue.text: Beat interrupts writers in old clubs

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

parts.note: nibs are pen points, the parts that write
to lick is to beat, as in 'we licked them'

explanation.surface: A drumbeat breaks in on authors meeting at their old clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The clubs are golf clubs, not gentlemen's clubs, and 'writers' are pen tips rather than authors.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old name for a golf club roughly like a nine iron.

clue.text: Sentimentality of school head avoiding dance

indicators.note: the word's head, its first letter, stays away

parts.note: SCH is a standard abbreviation of school
head = master, abbreviated M; 'head' is doing double duty

explanation.surface: A school's headteacher staying away from the sentimental school dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The M is the loose spot: solvers at the time read 'head' as master (M) as well as the deletion signal. SCH + M + (W)ALTZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltz is excessive sentimentality, especially in music or film.

clue.text: Intermittently, scout in Verdun shot straight

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked, so its letters are rearranged
put the scout letters inside the Verdun letters

parts.note: VERDUN rearranged, split around the inserted letters: UN…RVED

indicators.note: something intermittent comes and goes, so the letters of 'scout' appear only every other place

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of sCoUt

explanation.surface: A scout at the battlefield of Verdun fires a straight shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot straight' reads as firing accurately, but 'shot' rearranges VERDUN and 'straight' is the definition. UN + CU + RVED.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym built by negation: a line without any curve is by definition a straight one.

clue.text: Has a king's backing about British stronghold in North Africa

indicators.note: to back is to move backwards, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: K is king in chess notation
B is British, as on car stickers

explanation.surface: A king supports a British fort in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: HAS A K turned round is KASAH; B goes in the middle: KAS-B-AH.
explanation.definitionFit: A kasbah is the fortified citadel of a North African town.

clue.text: Bye-bye old Sue's poorly pets?

indicators.note: the letters are in a bad way, so they get rearranged

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to old Sue's sick animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pets' looks like animals, but here it means favourites, as in teacher's pets. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-eyed boys are favourites who can do no wrong, someone's pets.

clue.text: Deal with some theatre attendants

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used

explanation.surface: Handling some of the ushers at a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between the two words, which is where hidden words usually sit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a book that treats a subject deals with it, and a doctor treats or deals with a patient.

clue.text: Active old criminal's hedonistic life

indicators.note: criminal letters are bent, so rearranged

explanation.surface: An energetic old crook living a life of pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun, the old crook, but it is an adjective telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: La dolce vita, Italian for 'the sweet life', means a life of luxury and pleasure.

clue.text: Of which a draw ahead of others constitutes a win?

definitions.text: Of which a draw ahead of others constitutes a win?

parts.note: the surface wants a tied game; the setter means being pulled out of a hat

parts.words: ahead of others constitutes a win
parts.note: a draw beating other results sounds like a sporting paradox; in a raffle the first tickets drawn take the prizes

explanation.surface: A game, perhaps chess or football, where a draw beats the other results.
explanation.walkthrough: A draw usually means neither side wins; in a raffle, being drawn before the other tickets is winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffle tickets are drawn from a hat, and the first ones drawn win prizes.

clue.text: Where vigilant Customs official might look, however

definitions.text: Where vigilant Customs official might look
definitions.meaning: a thorough officer checks every piece of luggage, not just a chosen few
an everyday adverbial phrase meaning 'anyway' or 'be that as it may'

explanation.surface: A customs officer deciding where to search, however.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: a thorough customs officer might look in any case (suitcase).
explanation.definitionFit: In any case means however, whatever happens.

clue.text: Juliet's lot permits supporting better university

indicators.note: in a down clue, a support sits underneath

parts.note: to cap something is to better it

explanation.surface: Juliet's family grants permission that helps a better university.
explanation.walkthrough: LETS goes below CAP + U in the down answer. 'Better' is a verb, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Capulets are Juliet's family in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: On which you'd log who arses about

indicators.note: the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A diary where you record someone who messes around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Log' looks like record-keeping; here it means cutting logs. To arse about is British slang for messing around.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawhorse is a frame that holds wood while you saw it into logs.

clue.text: Annual study period in America mostly decays, unfortunately

indicators.note: most of the word: the last letter goes
the letters meet an unlucky jumbling

explanation.surface: A year of study in America goes to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In America' looks like the setting, but AMERICA is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The academic year is the yearly period of school or university teaching.

clue.text: Chinese system, one-third Taoism and two-thirds I Ching

indicators.note: the first third of the word's letters
the first two-thirds of the letters

parts.note: the first two of TAOISM's six letters
the first four of ICHING's six letters

explanation.surface: A Chinese philosophy blending Taoism and the I Ching.
explanation.walkthrough: Taoism and the I Ching are both Chinese; the surface stays in the same world as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tai chi is a Chinese system of slow exercise and martial art.

clue.text: One's boring coat

definitions.note: 'One's boring' describes a person, so it stands for the noun ANORAK
definitions.meaning: British slang for a dull, obsessive enthusiast

explanation.surface: Someone's dull coat.
explanation.walkthrough: An anorak is British slang for a dull, obsessive enthusiast. 'One's boring' means someone who is boring.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a hooded waterproof jacket, and also a nerdy bore.

clue.text: Released single?

definitions.meaning: unfastened, as a horse from a cart
getting hitched is slang for marrying, so an unmarried person has not been

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is playful: getting hitched is marrying, so someone single is unhitched.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhitched means released from a hitch, as a horse from a cart.

clue.text: Mean to investigate Guy's Hospital Trust, initially

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: An intention to look into a London hospital trust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, intend; it is the adjective, stingy. Guy's is a hospital in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for stingy: a tight or mean person hates parting with money.

clue.text: Long thread about End of Empire

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A long-running story about the end of the Empire, or of Empire magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb, to yearn. Empire is italic as the film magazine's title. YARN goes around E: YE-ARN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, but only once 'long' is read as the verb meaning to crave, not the adjective.

clue.text: Infuriate a Green liberal

indicators.note: letters treated liberally are set free to move

explanation.surface: Annoying a Green who is also a Liberal, a political squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green liberal' looks like a politician; 'liberal' only means freely rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to fill someone with rage or fury.

clue.text: One wooing Macron upset former queen

indicators.note: letters upset are knocked into a new order

parts.note: ER = Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: President Macron courting a former queen and upsetting her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as the French president annoying a queen, but it only rearranges MACRON.
explanation.definitionFit: A romancer is someone who woos or courts.

clue.text: Tracks onset of sudden change in USA

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Following an abrupt shift in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' is coins, not alteration. 'Tracks' is a verb: a dog scents its quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: To scent is to track by smell.

clue.text: * skater is all over the place

indicators.note: the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A skater, marked with a star, is sprawling everywhere on the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the symbol itself, printed at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is the symbol itself rather than a word, a rare trick; its name comes from Greek for 'little star'.
